claims: The United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) is a federal law enforcement agency.
USPIS protects the U.S. Mail system, employees, and customers.
Postal Inspectors investigate over 200 federal crimes.
Over 1,200 Postal Inspectors enforce federal laws related to the postal system.
Over 1,200 Postal Inspectors work with U.S. Attorneys to prosecute cases.
Requirements to become a Postal Inspector include U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent resident status.
Requirements to become a Postal Inspector include being generally between 21 and 37 years old.
Requirements to become a Postal Inspector include a four-year degree from an accredited institution.
Exceptions to the education requirement for Postal Inspector exist for veterans.
Requirements to become a Postal Inspector include no felony or domestic violence convictions.
Requirements to become a Postal Inspector include good physical condition.
Requirements to become a Postal Inspector include a valid driver's license.
USPIS applications are accepted through their hiring portal.
